newsitem.title: CANADA: Nortel to hire 5,000 in major Canada expansion.
newsitem.headline: Nortel to hire 5,000 in major Canada expansion.

text.p: Canada's Northern Telecom Ltd. said on Friday it will hire 5,000 workers over the next four years in the Ottawa area as part of a C$250 million ($181 million) expansion.
In one of its biggest such moves in years, Nortel, the world's sixth largest telecommunications equipment supplier, will expand its research and development facilities in Canada's capital region.
"Our growth in Canada is a direct result of our success internationally," Nortel President John Roth said in a statement.
Nortel, 51.5 percent-owned Canada's largest publicly traded firm BCE Inc., already employs 10,000 people in the Ottawa area and 68,000 worldwide. It posted 1996 revenues of $12.8 billion.
The company said most of the recruits would be skilled in computer science, software development, electrical engineering and other technology specialties.

Nortel technology division president Gedas Sakus said in a telephone interview that "this is only one of a series of expansions that we have under way in our corporation. We're targeting our business to grow about 15 percent in revenue per annum or better."
Nortel posted annual sales growth of 20 percent in the past few years, mostly from growing global demand as countries throw open their telecommunications industries to international competition.

Eagle & Partners technology analyst Emil Savov said that Nortel's expansion reflected explosive demand in mobile communications such as cellular telephones, and data traffic from increased Internet usage.
Mobile phone use was forecast to jump to 590 million subscribers by the end of 2001 from 137 million in 1996, according to a study released this week by Swedish telecommunications firm LM Ericsson.
Savov added that Internet users were copying data and information from sites to their own computers at increasing rates.
